name: Grouping of Identical Figures
shortcutSummary: Identify which figures are rotations of each other (identical when rotated) and group them. Figures that require flipping (mirror image) are NOT identical — they are different.
conceptExplanation: Grouping of Identical Figures questions present several figures and ask you to identify which ones are identical (same figure, possibly rotated) and which are different (mirror images or distinct shapes).

subtopics.name: Grouping of Identical Figures — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation: Grouping of Identical Figures questions present several figures and ask you to identify which ones are identical (same figure, possibly rotated) and which are different (mirror images or distinct shapes).
shortcuts: Rotation vs Reflection: Rotation preserves handedness; reflection (mirror) reverses it.
Fixed Feature Tracking: Pick a distinctive feature and track its relative position after rotation.
Count and Compare: If two figures have different element counts, they cannot be identical.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Group the given nine figures into three classes based on common characteristics:

9 figures are given: 1, 2, 3 are rectilinear polygons (Triangle, Square, Pentagon); 4, 5, 6 are curved closed shapes (Circle, Ellipse, Oval); 7, 8, 9 are intersecting crossed lines.
practiceQuestions.hint: Find the 3 distinct defining characteristics that can partition the 9 figures into 3 equal sets of 3.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Figures 1, 2, 3 form a group of straight-line polygons. Figures 4, 5, 6 form a group of curved closed figures. Figures 7, 8, 9 form a group of open intersecting line pairs.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Identify recurring visual properties (e.g. line type, nesting, shading).
Step 2: Form candidate triplets that share the exact same property.
Step 3: Ensure all 9 figures are exhausted without overlap to get (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6), (7, 8, 9).

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Group the given nine figures into three classes based on common characteristics:

9 figures: 1, 4, 7 each have one figure enclosed inside another identical figure; 2, 5, 8 each have two figures bisected by a line; 3, 6, 9 each have three concentric shapes.
practiceQuestions.hint: Find the 3 distinct defining characteristics that can partition the 9 figures into 3 equal sets of 3.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Group (1, 4, 7) share the attribute of a shape nested inside an identical shape. Group (2, 5, 8) are divided into equal halves by a bisector. Group (3, 6, 9) have concentric nested structures.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Identify recurring visual properties (e.g. line type, nesting, shading).
Step 2: Form candidate triplets that share the exact same property.
Step 3: Ensure all 9 figures are exhausted without overlap to get (1, 4, 7), (2, 5, 8), (3, 6, 9).
